```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

#read in data, should not show up on dashboard

library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

#data.fivethirtyeight.com / silver bulletin
#for prediction using data

# install.packages("fivethirtyeight")
library(fivethirtyeight)

candy <- fivethirtyeight::candy_rankings
# candy
candy <- candy |>
  mutate(type =
                case_when(
                          chocolate & fruity ~ "both", # ORDER MATTERS
                          chocolate ~ "chocolate",
                          fruity ~ "fruity",
                          .default = "other"
                          )
         )

# count(candy, type)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
### sorting candy by win % for futher usage
# needs dplyr for "select()" function
library(dplyr)

candySorted <- candy

candySorted <- candySorted %>%
  arrange(desc(winpercent)) %>%
  select(
    competitorname,
    type,
    winpercent,
    sugarpercent,
    pricepercent
  )
```

# Top Candies

## Row 1 {.tabset}

```{r}
#| title: "Top 5 Head-to-Head - 'Chocolate VS Fruity' by Win Percentage"

# filters sorted candy by win %  by only chocolate, AND takes only top 5
topFiveChoco <- filter(candySorted, type == "chocolate") %>%
  slice(1:5)
# topFiveChoco

# filters sorted candy by win %  by only fruity, AND takes only top 5
topFiveFruity <- filter(candySorted, type == "fruity") %>%
  slice(1:5)
# topFiveFruity

# combines the two datasets
combinedTopFiveVS <- bind_rows(topFiveChoco, topFiveFruity) %>%
  arrange(desc(winpercent))
# combinedTopFiveVS


vsPlot <- ggplot(combinedTopFiveVS, aes(
  x = reorder(competitorname, -winpercent), 
  y = winpercent,
  fill = type,
  text = paste0(
    "Candy: ", competitorname, "<br>",
    "Win %: ", round(winpercent, 2), "%<br>",
    "Sugar Percentile: ", round(sugarpercent * 100, 2), "%<br>",
    "Price Percentile: ", round(pricepercent * 100, 2), "%"
  )
)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("chocolate" = "brown",
                               "fruity" = "green")) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 5 Head-to-Head: 'Chocolate VS Fruity' by Win Percentage",
    x = "Candy",
    y = "Win Percentage (%)",
    fill = "Candy Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggplotly(vsPlot, tooltip = "text")
```


# Scatter + Boxplot

```{r}
#| title: "Candy type win % boxplot + scatter plot"

# making combined boxplot and scatter plot
myBoxPlot <- ggplot(candy, aes(type,
                               winpercent,
                               color = type,
                               fill = type)
                    ) +
  # set botplot to slight transparency to see jitter
  geom_boxplot(aes(alpha = 0.2)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(text = paste("Candy Name:", competitorname,"<br>",
                               "Win Percent:", round(winpercent, 1), "%")
                  # TODO: width for cage of where points can display
                  )
              ) +
  # custom colors for candy types
  # color reference:  https://derekogle.com/NCGraphing/resources/colors
  scale_color_manual(values = c(chocolate = "brown",
                                fruity = "green4",
                                other = "darkgray",
                                both = "darkolivegreen")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(chocolate = "brown",
                               fruity = "green",
                               other = "gray",
                               both = "darkolivegreen")) +
  labs(title = "Candy type win %",
       x = "Types of Candies",
       y = "Win %")

ggplotly(myBoxPlot, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r}
  icon = "bag",

  ###number of rows in candy dataset (85)
  # value = count(candy, fruity == "TRUE") # 38; DOESN'T WORK SINCE IT OUTPUTS A TABLE, NOT A VALUE
  
  # value = nrow(candy[candy$fruity == "TRUE", ]) # 38; slow due to duplicating dataframe, AND if NA values exist, will be added to count
  
  value = sum(candy$type == "chocolate")
)
```

```{r}

#| title: "Number of Fruity Candies"

list(
  icon = "bag-fill",
  color = "success",
  ###number of rows in candy dataset (85)
  # value = count(candy, fruity == "TRUE") # 38; DOESN'T WORK SINCE IT OUTPUTS A TABLE, NOT A VALUE
  
  # value = nrow(candy[candy$fruity == "TRUE", ]) # 38; slow due to duplicating dataframe, AND if NA values exist, will be added to count
  
  value = sum(candy$type == "fruity") # 37 (Amber's solution); works because type is our newly made column that filters for 1) fruity + chocolate, 2) exclusively fruity, and 3) exclusively chocolate
  
  # value = sum(candy$fruity == "TRUE" & candy$chocolate == "FALSE", na.rm = TRUE) # 38 without the candy$chocolate condition, 37 with it

)
```

```{r}
               col.names = c("Candy",

                             "Win %",
                             "Sugar %",
                             "Price %"),
               caption = "All Candies"
  )
```
